payload.message: I think the agent is the problem. Port 457879 is invalid, so the agent drops the session, and after that the board just retries forever.

steps.label: Read the report and earlier results
Decoded every packet in the log

result.reply: The data disagrees on the port: the agent wrapped 457879 to 64663 and the session was established, so the port isn't why it closed. The agent also didn't drop it on its own; it received 36 zero bytes and treated them as a delete. After that the agent log shows only identical 13-byte packets arriving, which points at the board side.

parts.claim: Port 457879 is invalid and caused the session to fail.
parts.why: Agent wrapped the port to 64663, then received a create and established the session at 192.168.10.210:38908. The port path worked.

evidence.quote: [1707258509.431443] info     | SessionManager.hpp | establish_session        | session established    | client_key: 0x2A2ED975, address: 192.168.10.210:38908

parts.claim: The agent drops the session on its own, so the agent is the problem.
parts.why: The agent did close the session, but right after receiving a 36-byte all-zero packet, decoded as a delete. The trigger is the received data.

parts.claim: After the close the board retries forever.
parts.why: The agent received identical 13-byte packets about every 0.1 s (lines 18 to 34, nine in the log), not literally forever. The log is short. The retry logic is on the board, which this log can't see.

payload.message: Challenge: after round 2 points to H7 D-cache/DMA coherency, why did the first CREATE packet get through cleanly and only the second packet come out zeroed? If the DMA region setup were wrong, I would expect the create to be at risk too, unless the two sends use different buffers, pools or streams. That asymmetry looks like the key unexplained piece. What explains it, and how do we test it?

steps.label: Decoded every packet in the log
Read the report and earlier results

input.reply: The asymmetry is real, but it doesn't rule out a Tx-path fault. Cache and DMA faults depend on which buffer and cache state a send hits, and the agent log can't see either. The sends also differ: 24 bytes against 36. Log buffer addresses and regions for both write callbacks.

parts.claim: The clean first CREATE and the zeroed second packet make a cache/DMA coherency fault unlikely.
parts.why: The agent received the first packet intact (24 bytes) and the second as 36 zero bytes. Coherency faults depend on buffer and cache state, so asymmetry alone doesn't exclude one, but it needs explaining.

parts.claim: The two sends use different buffers, pools or streams, which would explain the asymmetry.
parts.why: The agent log shows only received length and content (24 vs 36 bytes). It cannot show which board buffer, pbuf pool or memory region each send used.
parts.observed_at: agent log on the host; board not observed
